Run address-review on my merge request https://git.acme.dev/payments/ledger/-/merge_requests/214. I pasted what it shows below.

Title: Retry failed webhook deliveries
Description: Implements PAY-412. Deliveries that fail with a 5xx or a timeout are retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff, and every attempt is recorded in `delivery_attempts`.
Linked ticket PAY-412: Retry webhook deliveries that fail with a 5xx response or a timeout, up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff, and record every attempt. Out of scope: the delivery dashboard, and email and SMS notifications.
Changed files: `webhooks/deliver.go`, `webhooks/retry.go`, `webhooks/retry_test.go`, `db/migrations/0042_delivery_attempts.sql`. The repo's CONTRIBUTING.md covers formatting and commit messages only.

Open review threads, none answered yet:
1. Dana on `webhooks/retry.go:41`: "nit: `backoff` doubles with no cap, so attempt 5 waits 16 minutes. The delivery worker's lease is 10 minutes, so another worker takes the job mid-wait and sends the same webhook again."
2. Lee on `webhooks/deliver.go:52`: "must change: please use a `switch` on the status code instead of this if/else chain. I find switches easier to read."
3. Dana on `webhooks/retry.go:18`: "Typo in the doc comment: 'exponental'."
4. Lee on `webhooks/retry_test.go:1`: "suggestion: only the 5xx path has a test. Can you add one for the timeout path?"
5. Priya on `webhooks/deliver.go:30`: "Retrying in-process with a sleep means every deploy drops the pending retries. I think retries belong on the job queue we already use for emails. Can you sketch how that would look? We need to settle this before merge."
6. Priya on `db/migrations/0042_delivery_attempts.sql:3`: "Why is `attempt_no` a SMALLINT and not an INT?"
7. Lee on `webhooks/deliver.go:5`: "FYI: the platform team moves all outbound HTTP to a shared client next quarter."

There are no other comments.
cases.tests: Labels every open comment on its merit, shows the reviewer's label beside its own where they differ, proposes a new label when none fits, keeps the investigation shallow, and waits for the user's decisions.
traps: Comment 1 is marked 'nit' by its reviewer but describes duplicate deliveries, comment 2 is marked 'must change' but is a matter of taste, and comment 4's 'suggestion' is close in meaning to its label but not the same word.
Comment 7 asks for nothing and fits none of the labels.
Comment 5 asks for a sketch of the job-queue approach, a lure toward designing it during triage.
expectations: Labels comment 3 (the typo) as nit, comment 4 (the missing timeout test) as should change, comment 5 (in-process retries versus the job queue) as blocker, and comment 6 (SMALLINT) as question.

Labels comment 1 as must change although the reviewer wrote 'nit', and comment 2 as personal preference although the reviewer wrote 'must change', and shows the reviewer's own label next to its own on comments 1, 2 and 4 ('nit', 'must change' and 'suggestion').

Says that no label fits comment 7, rather than labeling it nit, personal preference, should change, must change, blocker or question, and proposes a new label for that kind of comment for the user to add to the list.

Keeps the investigation shallow: for comment 5 it gives a rough size for moving retries to the job queue and leaves the sketch the reviewer asked for until after the user decides, instead of writing it out now.
Ends by asking the user to decide each comment, and changes, pushes or posts nothing.

cases.prompt:
Continue address-review on my merge request https://git.acme.dev/payments/ledger/-/merge_requests/214. Its ticket, PAY-412, retries webhook deliveries that fail with a 5xx or a timeout, up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff; email and SMS notifications are out of scope. This session has write access to the merge request and to the PAY tracker.

Your previous message presented four open comments:
1. must change (Dana wrote 'nit'), `webhooks/retry.go:41`: `backoff` doubles with no cap, so attempt 5 waits 16 minutes, past the worker's 10-minute lease, and another worker sends the webhook again. Recommend: fix in this merge request by capping the wait at 5 minutes.
2. should change, Lee, `webhooks/deliver.go:48`: add retries to email notifications in `notify/email.go`. Recommend: defer, because PAY-412 puts email out of scope.
3. personal preference (Lee wrote 'blocking'), `webhooks/deliver.go:52`: use a `switch` instead of the two-branch if/else chain. Recommend: disagree.
4. question, Priya, `db/migrations/0042_delivery_attempts.sql:3`: why SMALLINT and not INT for `attempt_no`? Recommend: answer that attempts stop at 5, so SMALLINT holds every value.

The current code in `webhooks/retry.go`:
```go
const maxAttempts = 5

// backoff returns the wait before the given attempt.
func backoff(attempt int) time.Duration {
	return 30 * time.Second << attempt
}
```

My reply: "1 fix, 2 defer, 3 I disagree, 4 answer it. Go ahead."
cases.tests: Turns the user's decisions into an exact diff and ticket text for approval, holds the replies until the push and the ticket exist, and gets a reason for the disagreement.
traps: 'Go ahead' approves the decisions before any diff, ticket or reply text exists.
The disagreement with comment 3 comes without a reason.
The earlier recommendation and the reply say only 'defer'; neither names a follow-up ticket.
expectations: Makes the backoff cap for comment 1 itself and shows its exact diff, asking for approval before pushing it.
Shows the full text of a follow-up ticket for the email-retries comment and asks for approval before creating it.
Treats 'Go ahead' as approval of the decisions, not of any diff or text: it reports nothing as pushed, created, posted or resolved.
Gets a reason for disagreeing with comment 3 from the user, by asking for it or proposing one for the user to confirm, so the reply can state it.
Holds the reply to comment 1 until the fix is pushed and the reply to comment 2 until the ticket exists to link; it posts no reply in this message.

cases.prompt:
Continue address-review on my merge request https://git.acme.dev/payments/ledger/-/merge_requests/214. This session can post and resolve on the merge request. I approved your diff and ticket: you pushed commit `7f3c9e1`, which caps the backoff at 5 minutes, and created PAY-431 (https://tracker.acme.dev/browse/PAY-431) for email retries. The decided comments:

1. Dana on `webhooks/retry.go:41`: "Great work overall! nit: `backoff` doubles with no cap, so attempt 5 waits 16 minutes, past the worker's 10-minute lease, and another worker sends the same webhook again." Decision: fix.
2. Lee on `webhooks/deliver.go:48`: "While you're here: email notifications fail the same way. Can you add retries to `notify/email.go` too?" Decision: defer.
3. Lee on `webhooks/deliver.go:52`: "blocking: please use a `switch` on the status code instead of this if/else chain. I find switches easier to read." Decision: I disagree. My reason: "Honestly, it's not that I dislike switches — it's that every other handler in webhooks/ checks the status with if/else (I went through all six), and this chain has only two branches, so a switch adds lines without making anything clearer."
4. Priya on `db/migrations/0042_delivery_attempts.sql:3`: "Why is `attempt_no` a SMALLINT and not an INT?" Decision: answer. My answer: attempts stop at 5 (`maxAttempts`), so SMALLINT holds every value, and the table grows by about 40 million rows a month, so the smaller column saves space.
cases.tests: Drafts one reply per decision for approval: the fix names its commit, the deferral links its ticket, the disagreement gives the author's reason and keeps its thread open, and every reply follows the skill's reply rules.
traps: Dana's comment opens with praise, a lure toward a thank-you opener.
The author's reason uses an 'Honestly' opener, an em dash and a 'not X but Y' contrast, lures for copying them into the reply.
expectations: Shows the exact text of all four replies and which threads it will resolve, and asks for approval before posting or resolving anything.
The reply to comment 1 says what changed and names commit 7f3c9e1, and the reply to comment 2 links PAY-431.
The reply to comment 3 gives the author's reason for keeping the if/else chain, and the plan leaves that thread open while resolving the threads of comments 1, 2 and 4.
Each reply is written as the author, in first person, and opens with its outcome (the fix, the ticket, the disagreement or the answer) rather than with praise, thanks or a restatement of the comment.
No reply contains an em or en dash, a 'not X but Y' contrast, an 'Honestly' opener, or a sign-off such as 'Hope this helps'.
